title: Celebrity Autobiography on Broadway #celebrityautobiography #broadway...
transcript: Kicking off the 2026-2027 Broadway season is a show highly anticipated by maybe a dozen people. The concept is simple — a group of celebrities read excerpts from other celebrities’ autobiographies, word for word in comedic fashion. While this isn't something I'd personally ever be itching to see on a Broadway stage, I can see the potential entertainment value. Unfortunately though, it simply wasn't that funny. Sure, some of the material they pulled was inherently ridiculous, but a lot of it was pretty mundane and relied on someone who could elevate the material and characterize it a little more. Jeff Hiller was the only cast member at my performance who truly did this and he was by far the highlight of the show for me. Other folks did the assignment perfectly fine such as Leslie Kritzer and Jackie Hoffman, but there were a few cast members who really couldn't find a way to make it funny at all. I think I felt secondhand embarrassment more times than I laughed out loud, but it's not like it was painful. If there's someone in the cast you're dying to see, knock yourself out. I was glad my ticket was comped, but I still paid with my time. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer explicitly says it wasn't funny, felt secondhand embarrassment more than laughs, and was glad the ticket was comped. Only mild praise for one cast member prevents this from being a full pan.
keyQuote: I think I felt secondhand embarrassment more times than I laughed out loud
